QF.id: IV Introduction to Interest Rate Derivatives_16

question.text: As per the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, exchange-traded derivative contracts are legal and valid if they are:

answer.text: Traded on a recognized stock exchange and settled through its clearing house
Documented and signed by both parties

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 18A of SC(R)A provides that exchange-traded derivative contracts are legal and valid when they are (1) traded on a recognized stock exchange and (2) settled on the clearing house of that exchange, in accordance with its rules and bye-laws. The workbook also notes a separate Section 18A clause covering contracts between such parties and on such terms as may be notified by the Central Government. The Trap: The Section 18A test applies to exchange-traded contracts (and notified inter-party contracts); it is not a general validity test for OTC derivatives. Note: For ETIRD, the recognized-exchange-and-clearing-house route is the relevant Section 18A condition.
